messages:
Maria Chen: thinking about toggling per-signal pipelines for agents — lightweight per-signal vs shared pipeline debate. would love quick opinions on UX and routing/quota implications. example: spans from mobile with short retention vs logs with long retention. should console default to shared and surface a per-signal override? @Sophie Li @Ajay Singh

Ajay Singh: +1 default shared. per-signal pipelines explode memory + exporter fanout. but spans sometimes need different kv cache semantics. idea: create per-signal only when retention or routing differs significantly. lazy-create + GC? :thinking_face:

Sophie Li: agree on lazy-create. important: we need lifecycle hooks to garbage-collect idle pipelines or metrics will blow up. also console must show estimated cost before you flip the toggle (eg egress, exporter count).

Kevin Patel: one mitigation is soft-quotas at gateway that throttle or drop low-priority signal traffic rather than spawn a pipeline. cheaper operationally. still, for low-latency spans you might want a dedicated pipeline. tradeoff matrix needed.

infra-bot: deploy requested: collector/auto-pipeline-gc v1 pushed to canary (sha: ab12cd)

Maria Chen: quick mock config for the console toggle so we're aligned:
```
collector.routing = {
  mode: "shared",
  per_signal_overrides: ["spans"],
  retention_overrides: {"spans": "7d"}
}
```

Sophie Li: UX: show "estimated cost delta: +0.6x egress / +12% exporter-count" and an "explain" link that lists which exporters will fan out and which tenants are affected. also surface memory delta and GC timeout.

Ajay Singh: rollout plan idea: feature flag off by default, enable for 10 tenants (canary), monitor exporter_count_per_tenant, pipeline_memory, pipeline_count_idle. ramp if stable. alert if exporter_count_per_tenant > 8 or pipeline_count_idle > 50.

Maria Chen: action items: (1) Sophie - console toggle mock + cost calc (2) Ajay - GC + throttle/quota plan (3) Kevin - propose SLOs for per-signal pipelines. i'll schedule a 30m sync monday to review. thanks :thumbsup:

Kevin Patel: one question: can we avoid pipeline spawn by annotating incoming spans with retention tags at ingest and route in exporter side? sounds lighter-weight if exporters accept retention metadata.

Sophie Li: tagging is possible but we need a contract so exporters and storage understand retention metadata. follow-up: create a small compatibility doc and a migration plan.

Maria Chen: ok queued. will add docs + metrics to the Monday agenda.
